## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 decode on Blackwell with MegaMoE still has two serial pieces at the mHC layer boundaries:

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash does not run on A100 today: its attention, indexer and cache codecs need FlashMLA, DeepGEMM and FP8/FP4 conversion instructions that SM80 lacks; on H100, `main` runs it on its stock kernels. items.title: [RFC]: Packed-weight INT4 GEMM (W4A16 / W4A8) for RDNA4 (gfx1200/gfx1201)
items.author: jeffreylowzg
items.summary: Proposes repacking INT4 weights at load time into WMMA fragment order with interleaved scales for optimized HIP decode kernels on RDNA4 GPUs, achieving up to 2.3× throughput improvement.
items.body:
### Motivation.

items.title: [#21912][perf] Avoid full priority-queue scans for bounded peeks
items.author: Hang-get
items.summary: Priority scheduling with KV-balanced attention-DP admission calls every admitting iteration. The existing implementation scans the entire waiting queue even though the admission window is normally 32 requests.
items.body:
## Description

Priority scheduling with KV-balanced attention-DP admission calls `PriorityWaitingQueue.peek_requests` every admitting iteration. The existing `heapq.nsmallest` implementation scans the entire waiting queue even though the admission window is normally 32 requests.

Use a best-first frontier over the existing min-heap for bounded peeks. It visits only the relevant heap branches, reducing the bounded path from O(n log k) to O(k log k) without mutating or copying the source heap. Requests for at least one quarter of the queue retain the existing `nsmallest` path.

Closes #21912.

items.author: xsxszab
items.summary: Fixes a tensor-size mismatch in MRV2 pipeline parallelism where stages resolving different CUDA graph modes pad tokens differently and incorrectly copy oversized intermediate tensors.

Each pipeline stage resolves its CUDA graph mode from its own attention layers, so two stages can pad the same step to different token counts. items.title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Register host-backed KV pages over their full stride span
items.author: yeshihai
items.summary: Fixes NixlConnector rejecting host-resident padded KV pages by registering the full stride span instead of using cache.nbytes which truncates the last page.
items.body:
## Overview

`NixlConnector` rejects host-resident KV pools whose pages are padded to a kernel/packing alignment. Registration uses `cache.nbytes`, which stops short of the last page's stride, while the descriptor path addresses `num_blocks * block_stride`. This patch registers the full stride span for `is_host_resident` groups.

## Claims

- Fixes the startup failure `KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions ...` for host-resident, padded KV pages.
- Device-resident groups and unpadded host pages register exactly the same range as before; only padded host-resident groups change

items.title: [Fix] hicache: retain prefetched host pages until admission
items.author: zeyuan-lcl
items.summary: In cache mode, a completed L3 prefetch inserts pages into the host radix tree before request admission but does not retain an eviction reference. Under L2 pressure, a later prefetch can evict those pages before load-back.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes [#49221](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/49221).

In cache mode, a completed L3 prefetch inserts pages into the host radix tree before request admission but does not retain an eviction reference. Under L2 pressure, a later prefetch can evict those pages before load-back. The request then gets a partial hit or miss at admission despite the earlier storage hit, causing redundant prefill and increasing `cache_admission_shortfall`.

## Modifications

- Retain a host eviction reference after a prefetch completes. Release it after prefill admission or decode load-ba

## Summary

On Kimi-K3.1-Pro with a replicated DSpark draft under DCP8, a draft page contains **5 MiB** but reserves a **22.6875 MiB** shared-pool block. Target KV is still sharded; the replicated draft limits the capacity gain.

This adds a concrete TP8/DCP8 case to the existing hybrid-grouping discussion in #58638. The packed planner chooses repeats using layer-count padding; that objective can leave the shared pool oversized for the draft bucket.

items.title: [Fix] minicpm5: Recover malformed parameter boundaries
items.author: cyxu0401
items.summary: When a complete MiniCPM5 function block omits a parameter's, the XML fallback can consume the next parameter as part of the previous value or drop a required argument. For example: This change recovers.
items.body:
## Motivation

When a complete MiniCPM5 function block omits a parameter's `</param>`, the XML fallback can consume the next parameter as part of the previous value or drop a required argument. For example:

```xml
<function name="get_weather"><param name="city">Beijing<param name="date">2024-06-27</param></function>
```

This change recovers `{"city": "Beijing", "date": "2024-06-27"}`. It also preserves literal `</param>` inside complete CDATA when another malformed value forces fallback. These are deterministic parser regressions; this PR makes no claim about their frequency in model outputs

items.author: 2Zest

## Description

Incremental detokenization can produce output tokens whose text delta is empty (for example, the first two tokens of a multi-token Unicode character). items.author: BESzbing

Humming's W4A16 GEMM silently returns wrong output for group sizes that do not align with its 128-row K tiles. `HummingLinearKernel.can_implement` accepted every group size, so a bf16 GPTQ layer with G=96 and K=384 selected Humming and computed with the wrong scales. Fixes #66437.

items.title: [ROCm] wvSplitK: give N=5 the same unroll as N=4 on the YTILE=4 tile
items.author: XiaobingSuper
items.summary: On the generic tile table, takes the row, where gets and every other N falls through to. At N=5 that instantiation spills, which makes N=5 — the speculative-decode batch — about 4x slower than N=4 on large projections.
items.body:
## Overview

On the generic `wvSplitK` tile table, `out_dim > 12 * 4 * CUs` takes the `YTILE=4` row, where
`N == 4` gets `UNRL=1` and every other N falls through to `UNRL=2`. At N=5 that instantiation
spills, which makes N=5 — the speculative-decode batch — about 4x slower than N=4 on large
projections. This routes N=5 to `UNRL=1` as well: `__N == 4` -> `__N >= 4`.

- 3.9x to 4.3x on `wvSplitK` at N=5 with `out_dim > 12288` on MI355X (e.g. a 28672x4096 bf16
  projection: 167us -> 40.6us).

items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Fixes a race where non-streaming sessions freed image features while an unfinished child turn was still prefilling against them.
items.body:
Follows #49204, which removed the session `replace` parameter.

## Problem

Session turns skip the per-request media cleanup: a later turn's prompt contains the earlier turns' images, so the session keeps those features and frees them when it closes. The close deferred only for a streaming session with a turn in flight. A non-streaming session closed at once, explicitly or by the timeout reaper, and freed the features while a turn that reads them was still queued or prefilling.

## Fix

- `_has_live_readers(session)` is true while the streaming turn is in flight or an unfinished turn holds med

items.body:
### The feature, motivation and pitch

Python HTTP `/inference/v1/generate` supports `output_mode: derender` with `parse_context` for Chat. In that mode, the decode worker runs incremental BPE detokenization, stop strings, reasoning parsers, and tool-call parsers in one pass.

By contrast, `vllm-rs` HTTP `/inference/v1/generate` supports `tokens` only. On gRPC, `vllm.Inference` (`output_text = true`) emits raw `text` without output parsers or decoded `logprobs` candidate text (`CandidateTokenInfo`). Gateways that render prompts once at ingress (`vllm.Render/Tokenize`, #64685, #65503) need work

items.title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Keep CLIP and SigLIP special tokens for chat text embeddings
items.author: Alex-Wengg
items.summary: Adds CLIP and SigLIP-specific Jinja chat templates to preserve BOS/EOS special tokens in dual-encoder chat text embeddings.
items.body:
## Overview

On CLIP and SigLIP, text sent to `/v1/embeddings` as `messages` loses the special tokens its tokenizer adds, so it returns a different embedding than the same text sent as `input`. Chat requests default to `add_special_tokens=False`, and both models fall back to `template_basic.jinja`, which only joins the message text: CLIP loses BOS and EOS, SigLIP loses EOS.

This adds `template_clip.jinja` (BOS + text + EOS) and `template_siglip.jinja` (text + EOS; SigLIP defines no BOS), and drops the now-wrong `--chat-template template_basic.jinja` from the SigLIP example. Image-only request

items.title: [Fix] mamba: Preserve completed checkpoints across overlap gaps
items.author: CHiSwsz
items.summary: Non-lazy checkpointing can overwrite a completed Mamba/KDA checkpoint after a prefill gap under overlap scheduling. The next decode destination normally rotates in anticipation of a boundary.
items.body:
## Motivation

Non-lazy `extra_buffer` checkpointing can overwrite a completed Mamba/KDA checkpoint after a prefill gap under overlap scheduling. The next decode destination normally rotates in anticipation of a boundary. When that rotation is missed, processing the completed boundary records its slot and length but can leave the next write destination pointing at the same slot. A later boundary then overwrites the state while cache insertion still uses the earlier length.

items.author: Etelis
items.summary: At large sizes it is slow to set up: - The region is one file, so every worker pre-faults into the same file and page-cache inserts serialize. This splits the region across files, as already does (#59546), and maps the scheduler side without pre-faulting.
items.body:
## Purpose

Tiering keeps one shared CPU region per engine so its secondary tiers can address it. At large sizes it is slow to set up:

- The region is one `/dev/shm` file, so every worker pre-faults into the same file and page-cache inserts serialize.
- The scheduler then maps the whole region and pre-faults every page again, on one thread.

This splits the region across `REGION_SEGMENTS` files, as `CPUOffloadingSpec` already does (#59546), and maps the scheduler side without pre-faulting. Secondary tiers still see one contiguous range.

## [Core] Divergence-point prefix-cache salting: `cache_salt_start_idx`

### Motivation

`cache_salt` today is all-or-nothing. A salted request isolates its **entire**
block-hash chain, so two tenants on the same deployment never share a single
cached block — even when their prompts begin with the same thousands of tokens
(shared system prompts, RAG preambles, agent scaffolds). That is the
all-or-nothing tradeoff documented in "Governing the KV Cache: Preventing
Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference"
([arXiv:2608.09225](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09225)), which proposes sal

items.title: fix(tool_parsers): preserve trailing content in Hermes2ProToolParser
items.author: davrens101
items.summary: Fix streaming vs non-streaming content divergence in Hermes2ProToolParser. The streaming path preserved trailing text, so the two modes diverged and legitimate output after a tool call was lost. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
Fix streaming vs non-streaming content divergence in Hermes2ProToolParser.

## Problem
`Hermes2ProToolParser.extract_tool_calls` (non-streaming) kept only the text
preceding the first tool-call tag and silently dropped any trailing content
after the last tool call. The streaming path preserved trailing text, so the
two modes diverged and legitimate output after a tool call was lost.

## Fix
- Non-streaming: keep every part of the response outside tool-call tags as
  content (leading, between consecutive calls, and trailing).
- Streaming: emit trailing content after the last complete tool call

items.title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Bound cache-aware admission probe by request reuse limit
items.author: htang7415
items.summary: Fixes KV cache admission probe ignoring per-request prefix-cache reuse limits, causing incorrect queue ordering and unnecessary recomputation for scoring requests.
items.body:
## Overview

With `cache_aware_admission_window > 0`, the waiting-queue ranking probe
`KVCacheManager.get_num_cached_tokens` (added in #54625) estimates the hit with
`request.num_tokens - 1`. It ignores the request's prefix-cache reuse limit from
#60960. A prompt-scoring request with `prompt_logprob_start` is therefore ranked
by a resident prefix it is not allowed to adopt. It is admitted ahead of a peer
whose prefix it can actually reuse, and its fresh blocks evict that peer's
cached prefix. The probe now uses `request.get_max_cache_hit_length()`, the
same bound that actual adoption uses.

items.author: ruiling-smartbear
items.summary: runs the 32-layer V4.1 ViT once per image, and small images are launch-bound. On CUDA, images from every request in a prefill batch reach this call together, so the per-image passes add up under concurrency.
items.body:
## Motivation

`get_image_feature` runs the 32-layer V4.1 ViT once per image, and small images are launch-bound. On CUDA, images from every request in a prefill batch reach this call together, so the per-image passes add up under concurrency.

## Modifications

- `encode_images` packs up to 8 images per ViT pass, split by `cu_seqlens`, with per-image RoPE and aligner merge.
- Packing is used on `fa3`, `fa4` and `triton_attn`. SDPA ignores `cu_seqlens` metadata, so it and other backends keep the per-image path.
- CPU unit test: packed output equals per-image output across padding and pass bound

With the default overlap scheduler and `--enable-return-routed-experts`, DSpark rollouts return all-zero or stale routed-expert IDs for generated tokens. With routing replay in RL (Miles R3), the trainer replays these IDs, so generated tokens are trained through expert 0 instead of the experts the rollout actually used.

items.author: YaoleWu
items.summary: Mooncake zero-copy GET returns the number of bytes copied, so a positive result can still be a short read. Treating every positive result as a hit can expose an incompletely filled KV page or multimodal embedding.
items.body:
Mooncake zero-copy GET returns the number of bytes copied, so a positive result can still be a short read. Treating every positive result as a hit can expose an incompletely filled KV page or multimodal embedding. The embedding controller then promotes that entry from FILLING to READY. A truncated receipt vector can also leave entries unprocessed or acknowledge writes that were never confirmed.

- Require matching key/pointer/size counts and reject null or empty buffers before native I/O.
- Require GET bytes to equal the full destination siz

items.author: aoshen02

## Purpose

#64583 turned off the Kimi-K3 latent-MoE tail fusion whenever sleep mode is on, and logged a warning. At the time, level-2 sleep discarded the whole `weights` pool. The fusion's collective kernel keeps its state in that pool: the Lamport flags (`_routed_flags`, `_shared_flags`) and the peer pointer table. None of these are parameters, so they were lost on wake.

Since #66010, level 2 discards only allocations that hold nothing but parameters, and offloads and restores everything else at the same address. That state now survives sleep, so this PR removes the fallback and its warning

Mooncake PD cancellation can retire original request KV/cache locks, metadata or device destination slots before outstanding native writes are known to have drained. items.title: [Bugfix][Offload] Re-offload UVA params whose data replace_parameter rebound
items.author: suryakiranc
items.summary: Fixes UVA-offloaded parameters not being re-offloaded after replace_parameter rebonds.data to a new tensor on a different device.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #66264.

`replace_parameter` keeps the existing `Parameter` object (and its `_vllm_is_uva_offloaded` marker) and rebinds `.data` to the new device tensor when a repacked weight does not fit the old storage. `device_loading_context` only re-offloaded when the marker was missing, so these weights silently stayed resident on the device after `process_weights_after_loading`.

This change records each UVA-offloaded parameter's `data_ptr()` on entry and re-offloads if the marker is missing **or** the pointer changed. In-place copies (same pointer) are unaffected.

Related: #58178,

HiCache writes a prefix to L3 storage once, when it is first backed up to host. items.title: [Fix] benchmark: Honor max_completion_tokens in OpenAI datasets
items.author: weigangw
items.summary: OpenAI-format benchmark datasets silently discard: a row with is loaded with, and the chat benchmark then sends that incorrect limit back as. When both API fields are present, only the legacy is honored.
items.body:
## Motivation

OpenAI-format benchmark datasets silently discard `max_completion_tokens`: a row with `max_completion_tokens: 8` is loaded with `output_len=256`, and the chat benchmark then sends that incorrect limit back as `max_completion_tokens`. When both API fields are present, only the legacy `max_tokens` is honored.

items.title: Fix dataloader checkpoint directory creation on every writing rank
items.author: jwills
items.summary: When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts.
items.body:
When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts. A nonzero writing rank can therefore reach `torch.save` without its parent directory and fail.

Call `ensure_directory_exists` on every rank that writes a state file. Rank-independent loaders retain their rank-0-only writes. Extend the explicit-process-groups regression test, which uses DP rank 3, to assert that the parent directory exists.

items.body:

items.body:
## Description

Related to #21470. An oversized context can pass request admission and reach the V2 cache manager with a page-index table bounded by the physical pool. Enlarging that table alone changes the immediate sizing exception into repeated allocation failure, while increasing page-table memory, copy work, and exposure to existing 32-bit indexing limits.

Keep page-index staging bounded by the manager's allocatable sequence length and generation headroom. Supply the existing executor admission budget for ordinary dense, full-attention V2 target managers in aggregated serving with CP=1.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

An abort forces an active request to finish on its next step: the handler
sets the request's output length to its KV offset plus its query length, so
the next step's length check ends it. With speculative decoding (MTP), a

next step only when every draft is accepted. Otherwise it keeps its row, its

items.title: Cap eager speculative decode padding at max_tokens
items.author: lmcafee-nvidia
items.summary: Fixes a production bug where eager speculative decoding pads request counts beyond max_tokens, causing forward-pass shape mismatches in apply_rotary_emb_key.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With speculative decoding (MTP), an eager decode-only step pads its request
count up to a multiple of `REQUEST_ROUNDER` (4) and multiplies it by the
tokens each request carries. Unlike the non-speculative branch, it never caps
the result at `max_tokens`. When the rounded count times
`num_speculative_tokens + 1` exceeds `max_tokens`, the padded batch is larger
than the step's token buffers, and the forward fails in
`apply_rotary_emb_key()`.

This PR caps the padded decode request count at
`max_tokens // (num_speculative_tokens + 1)`. Eager speculative steps then

items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: When gradients can reach their accumulation placements without inner communication, MFSDP still allocates a packing buffer and copies gradients through it. Accumulate directly into instead, including HSDP/HFSDP with a singleton inner DP axis.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

When gradients can reach their accumulation placements without inner communication, MFSDP still allocates a packing buffer and copies gradients through it. Accumulate directly into `main_grad` instead, including HSDP/HFSDP with a singleton inner DP axis.

Each parameter group computes `requires_inner_reduction` from its existing mesh and gradient placements. Groups requiring communication retain the packed path. Other groups accumulate on compute in `main_grad.dtype`, avoiding communication-dtype

### What does this PR do?

Allow colocated NPU rollouts to explicitly select vLLM-Ascend's native IPC loading lifecycle. The trainer packs bounded byte buffers, exports a fresh IPC reference for each nonempty bucket, and waits for the worker to finish consuming that bucket. Leaving the option unset preserves the existing CUDA/ROCm, shared-memory and delta dispatch paths.

This is part 1 of a three-PR series: IPC, HCCL, then whole-stream reload.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

items.author: JonnesLin
items.summary: built its train/val s without a, so every iterator construction drew a from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted ru…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

How it happens:

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.

### What does this PR do?

Adds `sharded_nixl`, a checkpoint engine for disaggregated rollout with no trainer-side all-gather. Every trainer rank (FSDP or Megatron) exports only the shards it holds and NIXL-WRITEs them into the rollout workers' staging buffers. Each rollout worker reports what it loads (pipeline stage, resident experts and, for vLLM TP>1, its slice of each tensor) and receives only that. items.summary: Use for k3 KL estimates in the KL penalty, rollout rejection sampling, and off-policy diagnostics. The expression is mathematically equivalent to, but avoids subtracting 1 from an exponential close to 1.

### What does this PR do?

Use `torch.expm1(x) - x` for k3 KL estimates in the KL penalty, rollout rejection sampling, and off-policy diagnostics. The expression is mathematically equivalent to `exp(x) - 1 - x`, but avoids subtracting 1 from an exponential close to 1.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct `\boxed{0}` response scores 0 under `rm_type=math`. items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

`exec_and_wait` launches commands in detached sessions so they can survive transport retries, but its timeout and cancellation paths previously stopped waiting without stopping the detached command.

## Problem

A timed-out or cancelled sandbox command could keep running and mutate the sandbox after the caller had already moved on. There was also a race between launch acknowledgement and publishing the detached process group PID.

## Solution

- Record the detached session leader PID before executing the launcher.
- Wait for the PID marker before acknowledging a guarded spawn, i

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.
items.body:
## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

## Problem

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

## Summary

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

items.author: yuyz-cyber

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.title: require --ref-load when KL is enabled instead of crashing with a TypeError
items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.title: fix: reject non-positive rollout temperature at parse time
items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.
items.body:
## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.
